# General Spec Review Checklist: Migrate Database Migrations to Liquibase

**Purpose**: Author self-check of `spec.md` requirements quality before starting `/speckit-tasks` / `/speckit-implement` — general pass across completeness, clarity, consistency, and coverage.
**Created**: 2026-08-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is there a functional requirement covering the one-time local-volume cutover step, or does it exist only as an edge case and an assumption without a corresponding testable requirement? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec define what "documentation" means for FR-007 — README only, or also other docs (ADRs, onboarding guides, CI config comments)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK003 Is there a requirement addressing what happens if a changeset fails partway through (schema changeset succeeds, seed-data changeset fails) — beyond the general "fail startup clearly" language? [Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec define a naming/ordering convention future changesets must follow to preserve FR-004's ordering guarantee, or is that left fully unconstrained? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] — Resolved 2026-08-17: FR-004 now requires new changes to be appended, never edited/renumbered; Edge Cases bullet updated to point to it.
- [x] CHK005 Is the scope of SC-003's "search of the codebase" defined (e.g., source only, or also build artifacts, git history, CI configuration)? [Completeness, Spec §SC-003] — Resolved 2026-08-17: SC-003 now scopes the search to the current working tree, excluding VCS history.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "reproduce, exactly" in FR-002 clarified for non-deterministic seed values (e.g., `now()`-derived timestamps), or could it be read as requiring bit-for-bit identical output? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK007 Is "fail startup clearly" in FR-005 quantified with any observable signal (e.g., non-zero process exit, specific log marker), or left to reader interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005] — Already resolved via the earlier A1 fix (FR-005 defines "clearly" as non-zero exit + visible log failure); checkbox had not been re-marked until now.
- [x] CHK008 Is "clean-slate cutover" in the Assumptions section defined precisely enough to know what state counts as "clean," or does it rely on the reader inferring the mechanism? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK009 Is "correctly seeded database" in SC-001 given an objective definition (e.g., row counts, specific values), or is it only cross-referenced informally to FR-002? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §SC-001]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Are FR-001's "no other mechanism" language and the Constitution's Principle IV prohibition on ORM auto-DDL stated compatibly, with no gap in what's covered? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK011 Do the Assumptions section (only mentions "connection configuration and startup command unchanged") and the Edge Cases section (raises leftover schema-version tracking data) fully agree on what state a developer's existing environment may be in before cutover? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK012 Are User Story 1's acceptance scenarios and FR-003/FR-004 consistent about what "zero manual steps" covers on first run versus subsequent restarts? [Consistency, Spec §US1, §FR-003, §FR-004]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Can SC-002 ("100% of schema objects and seed rows... identical") be verified without prescribing a specific verification method, or does confirming it require assuming a particular tool/technique? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK014 Is SC-004 ("without re-applying any previously-applied change") independently verifiable from outside the system (e.g., observable log/state), or does it require inspecting internals not otherwise described in the spec? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK015 Does SC-003 specify a pass/fail threshold consistent with FR-006, or could a reviewer reasonably disagree on what counts as a "reference" to the previous tool (e.g., historical git commits vs. current tree)? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003, §FR-006] — Resolved 2026-08-17: same SC-003 scope edit as CHK005 (working tree, not history).

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK016 Is there an acceptance scenario for a developer who has NOT previously run the stack (true clean clone), distinct from the "already migrated, no volume" framing in US1's Independent Test? [Coverage, Spec §US1]
- [x] CHK017 Is there an acceptance scenario covering the case where documentation is updated but a secondary reference to the old tool is missed (partial completion of US3)? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §US3] — Resolved 2026-08-17: added US3 acceptance scenario 2 (every doc location must be updated consistently).
- [x] CHK018 Are there acceptance scenarios validating behavior when the backend restarts after a NEW changeset has been added (not just "no schema change" as in US1 scenario 3)? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §US1] — Resolved 2026-08-17: added US1 acceptance scenario 4; tasks.md T010a added.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK019 Does the spec define expected behavior when an already-applied changeset's content is modified after the fact (checksum drift), or is this left entirely to the Edge Cases bullet about startup failure in general? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-005] — Resolved 2026-08-17: added a dedicated Edge Cases bullet naming this scenario explicitly.
- [x] CHK020 Is there a stated expectation for concurrent startup (e.g., multiple backend instances applying changes at once), or is this explicitly out of scope? [Gap, Non-Functional] — Resolved 2026-08-17: added Assumption explicitly declaring single-instance/out-of-scope.
- [x] CHK021 Does the spec address what should happen if the previous tool's tracking table is present but the new tool's is not (mixed state described in Edge Cases) with a concrete expected outcome, or only a pointer to "Assumed clean-slate"? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK022 Is there any requirement bounding how long schema/seed application may take at startup, relative to the existing health-check timing the rest of the stack depends on? [Gap, Non-Functional] — Resolved 2026-08-17: added Assumption tying expected migration duration to the existing 30s healthcheck `start_period`.
- [x] CHK023 Does the spec state any requirement (or explicit non-requirement) around access control / secrets exposure for the new changelog files, given the seed data includes password hashes? [Gap, Non-Functional, Spec §Key Entities] — Resolved 2026-08-17: added Assumption stating the seed hashes are non-sensitive demo credentials with unchanged exposure level.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK024 Is the Assumption "no deployed environment with production data at stake" stated as validated fact or as an unverified assumption the author is asking a reviewer to confirm? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK025 Is the dependency on the changelog-format decision being deferred to planning (per Assumptions) clearly bounded, so a planner can't reintroduce a manual migration step under the banner of "implementation detail"? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-003]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK026 Is there any remaining ambiguity in FR-006 about whether "migration files belonging to the previous migration tool" includes compiled/build-output copies, or only source files? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK027 Is the relationship between the Key Entities' "Applied-Change History" and any data-retention/pruning expectation left fully unaddressed, and is that silence intentional (out of scope) or a gap? [Gap, Spec §Key Entities]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
